title: HRMS-Targeted-DIA Methodology for Quantification of Wastewater-Borne Pollutants
author: Gómez-Navarro, Labad, et al.
materials: column (100 × 2.1 mm i.d., 1.8 µm particle size) thermostated at 40 °C using a Waters ACQUITY UHPLC system (Waters, Milford, MA). For the detection, a Q-Exactive Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo-Fisher Scientific, Germany) equipped with heated electrospray ionization (HESI) was used. The tuning methods and parameters used for the MS acquisition were optimized in the following conditions; spray voltage was set to 3.5 kV (positive) and 2.5 kV (negative), S-Lens RF level, 60; capillary temperature, 350 °C; auxiliary gas temperature, 300 °C. Nitrogen was used as sheath gas flow rate 40; auxiliary gas flow rate 10 and sweep gas flow rate

steps.title: Prepare and condition SPE cartridge
steps.instruction: Assemble the homemade multi‑sorbent SPE cartridge with 200 mg Oasis HLB (upper layer) and a bottom layer containing 150 mg Bond Elut PPL, 100 mg WAX and 100 mg WCX. Condition the cartridge by passing 2 × 5 mL methanol followed by 2 × 5 mL HPLC‑grade water.

steps.title: Spike samples with isotopic standards
steps.instruction: Add the mixture of 80 isotopically labelled compounds to each 500 mL surface‑water aliquot before loading onto the SPE cartridge.

steps.title: Load sample onto SPE cartridge
steps.instruction: Pass the spiked 500 mL sample through the activated cartridge at approximately one drop every two seconds to achieve maximum retention of the analytes.

steps.title: Dry cartridge
steps.instruction: Dry the cartridge by passing a gentle air stream through it after the sample has been loaded.

steps.title: Elute analytes from cartridge
steps.instruction: Elute sequentially with (a) 2 × 3 mL 5 % NH₃ in MeOH:EtOAc (50:50 v/v), (b) 2 × 3 mL 2 % formic acid in MeOH:EtOAc (50:50 v/v), and (c) 3 mL MeOH:EtOAc (50:50 v/v), collecting an eluate of approximately 15 mL.

steps.title: Evaporate and reconstitute eluate
steps.instruction: Evaporate the eluate to dryness under a gentle nitrogen stream, then reconstitute in 500 µL H₂O:MeOH (95:5 v/v), giving a final concentration factor of 1000.

steps.title: Set up UHPLC system
steps.instruction: Install a Waters Acquity HSS T3 (C18) column (100 × 2.1 mm, 1.8 µm) thermostated at 40 °C on a Waters ACQUITY UHPLC system. Use an injection volume of 10 µL.

substeps.instruction: Mobile phase A: for ESI+ 5 mM NH₄Ac + 0.1 % formic acid in water; for ESI‑ 2 mM NH₄F in water.
Mobile phase B: acetonitrile for both ionization modes.

steps.title: Configure mass spectrometer parameters
steps.instruction: Set the Q‑Exactive Orbitrap with heated electrospray ionization. Use spray voltage 3.5 kV (positive) and 2.5 kV (negative), S‑Lens RF level 60, capillary temperature 350 °C, auxiliary gas temperature 300 °C, sheath gas flow 40 arb, auxiliary gas flow 10 arb, sweep gas flow 2 arb.

substeps.instruction: Full MS: resolution 70 000, AGC target 3 × 10⁶, maximum injection time 150 ms, scan range 90–1000 m/z.

Targeted‑DIA: resolution 17 500, AGC target 2 × 10⁵, injection time auto, loop count 1, Top N 10, isolation window 1.5 m/z, normalized collision energy 30 eV, inclusion list containing exact precursor masses, retention‑time windows and optimized collision energies.

steps.title: Acquire data with full‑scan and targeted‑DIA
steps.instruction: For each injection first acquire a full‑scan spectrum, then run the targeted‑DIA experiment using the predefined inclusion list to generate MS² spectra for the 116 target compounds.

steps.title: Identify and quantify analytes
steps.instruction: Apply SANTE 11,312/2021 criteria: accept a peak if signal‑to‑noise > 3, mass error ≤ 5 ppm, retention time within 0.1 min of the reference, and at least one product ion with mass error ≤ 5 ppm. Use the adduct ion from the full‑scan spectrum for the isotopically labelled internal standards.

steps.title: Prepare blanks and quality controls
steps.instruction: Process 500 mL of HPLC water through the entire SPE‑extraction‑reconstitution workflow to generate procedural blanks (no target peaks expected). Prepare QC samples by spiking the final extract solvent (95 % H₂O/5 % MeOH) to 50 µg L⁻¹ with the 116 target standards and the 80 isotopically labelled compounds; inject these QC samples together with the study samples.

steps.title: Generate matrix‑matched calibration curve
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10‑point calibration curve in the same solvent ratio as the final extracts, containing the 116 target standards and the 80 isotopically labelled compounds, and run it in the same sequence for quantification.

steps.title: Validate method (spiking study)
steps.instruction: Spike three 500 mL surface‑water aliquots at 5, 50 and 500 µg L⁻¹ (corresponding to 5, 50, 500 ng L⁻¹ after the 1000‑fold concentration) in triplicate. Process them as described above and use the data to evaluate recovery, matrix effect, precision, limits of detection/quantification and linearity.

steps.title: Calculate recovery rates
steps.instruction: Compute recovery (%) = [(Area_pre‑spiked – Area_blank) / (Area_post‑spiked – Area_blank)] × 100 for each compound.

steps.title: Calculate matrix effects
steps.instruction: Compute matrix effect (%) = {[(Area_matrix – Area_blank) / Area_solvent] – 1} × 100 for each compound at each validation level.

steps.title: Assess precision and detection limits
steps.instruction: Determine intra‑ and inter‑day relative standard deviation (RSD). Calculate method detection limit (MLOD) = 3 × SD_intercept / slope and method quantification limit (MLOQ) = 10 × SD_intercept / slope from the matrix‑matched calibration. Verify linearity (R² > 0.99) over 0.05–1000 µg L⁻¹.

description: Surface water pool samples were used for the method validation, and aliquots of 500 mL were spiked with the mix of the 116 selected targeted compounds. The method was validated, in triplicate, at three different concentration levels: 5, 50, and 500 μg l-1 in the extract, which would correspond to final sample concentrations of 5, 50, 500 ng l-1 respectively, after applying the method concentration factor of 1000. These concentrations were chosen in order to cover common environmental concentrations. The method was evaluated in terms of accuracy (recovery rates), matrix effect (ME), precision (% RSD), linearity (R2), method detection limits (MDL), method quantification limits (MQL) according to [10], for all three validated concentrations. In order to evaluate the accuracy of the method developed, recovery rates (RR) were calculated, for both intra and inter day precision. The recovery rates were calculated by comparing the peak area of the pool samples spiked before and after the method extraction.
